issue.title: Black screen and VSync problems on MacOS Mojave
issue.body:
Hi,

I have been playing with `go-gl/gl` and `go-gl/glfw` for some time now in my [rally-mka](https://github.com/mokiat/rally-mka) project.

Everything worked perfect up until I updated to MacOS Mojave. When I start the application, the screen is initially black. If I resize the window, the game starts to render to screen normally for around a second or two after which it goes black again.

Furthermore, the game speeds up drastically, as vsync does not seem to work.

(Yes, I am aware that timestamp deltas should be used for scene updates. The game is a port to Go of something I did many years ago, so its design is crap. 😅I just use it to experiment with and learn newer OpenGL versions and see how Go copes).

---

Issue #228 seems like a duplicate to this, however, I am using the latest version of `glfw` and the issue is not fixed for me. Furthermore, the vsync issue is not described there.

There is also pull request #219 where @kivutar mentions these problems, though I could not find them in GitHub issue tracker.

---

Is this related to OpenGL deprecation? My understanding was that it would continue to be supported for some time. Furthermore, the issue seems to be glfw related, and that project seems necessary even if one were to switch to Vulkan.

issue.title: Black screen on MacOS Mojave

repository.name: LearnOpenGL
repository.description: Code repository of all OpenGL chapters from the book and its accompanying website https://learnopengl.com

issue.body:
There's an issue with Mojave, which doesn't seem to have a clean solution and is not specific to your tutorial. All windows will display a completely black screen until you manually resize them, which is of course a bit tricky to do when the mouse is captured.

My workaround is to cmd-tab away, then press the maximize window button while holding the option key. It seems some others are to add a tiny bit of code to move the window or to downgrade XCode.

There's some discussion about this issue here:
https://stackoverflow.com/questions/52509427/mac-mojave-opengl

_Edit:_
The suggestion from user Qian_Lin on Stack Overflow worked okay for me. I put `glfwSetWindowPos(window, 100, 100);` in a run-once conditional at the bottom of my main loop.

Further discussion: https://github.com/glfw/glfw/issues/1334 and https://github.com/glfw/glfw/issues/1337

Comparing game engines and running the simple demo projects that ship with Godot 3.1 alpha 3, I was horrified to see that they nearly maxed the cpu on my high end mac laptop, kicking it into space heater mode.

It took months before I read a comment somewhere that this was related to an unbound render loop. I can't say I feel that that is anything but crazy in terms of how it will affect perception of the engine's general performance, which thus comes across as abysmal.

As someone who ardently supports open source, please, please consider changing the defaults so others don't come to this mistaken impression.

issue.title: Vsync is broken on macOS 10.14 Mojave

repository.name: allegro5
repository.description: The official Allegro 5 git repository. Pull requests welcome!

issue.body:
Apparently Apple broke vsync with OpenGL on Mojave.  See for example:
* https://github.com/glfw/glfw/issues/1337
* https://discourse.libsdl.org/t/sdl2-no-renderer-vsync-on-macos-mojave/25169
* (a zillion other GitHub issues on various repos that I don't feel like rounding up 😛)

The bug was reported against miniSphere by @rhuanjl; upon further iteration we discovered that neither setting `ALLEGRO_VSYNC` on the display, nor manually calling `al_wait_for_vsync()` immediately before flipping has any effect.  Then I took to Google and found out that this is apparently a widespread issue.

In SDL's case, the issue was able to be worked around by compiling with Xcode 9 instead of 10, but that doesn't seem to fix it for us.  So I figured I would report it here in case anyone else has any ideas.

issue.body:
Addresses issue #1337

Fixes VSync on macOS 10.14 (Mojave) by using CVDisplayLink to synchronize frames rather than setting NSOpenGLContextParameterSwapInterval.

Based on work for SDL by @rcgordon: https://hg.libsdl.org/SDL/rev/73f3ca85ac0e
